editorial_contributions.text:
This is the first in a series of papers which develops a theory of coding for a class of \(\mathbb Z^2\) subshifts of finite types (SFTs) that is similar to the theory available for \(\mathbb Z\) mixing SFTs. The main result is the following Theorem: 


For \(d\geq 2\), let \(X\) be a \(\mathbb Z^d\) subshift without periodic points and let \(Y\) be a \(\mathbb Z^d\) square mixing SFT containing a finite orbit. Suppose there is a homomorphism \(X\to Y\). Then, there exists an embedding \(X \hookrightarrow Y\) if and only if \(h(X)<h(Y)\). (It is also shown that for \(d=2\), a \(\mathbb Z^d\) square mixing SFT has finite orbits. Whether this is the case for \(d>2\) is an open problem.) 


The author also announces the following result from his forthcoming paper: 


If \(X\) is a \(\mathbb Z^2\) subshift without periodic points and if \(Y\) is a \(\mathbb Z^2\) square filling mixing SFT, then there exists a homomorphism \(X\to Y\). The two theorems together imply the following extension of Krieger's Embedding Theorem: 


Let \(X\) be a \(\mathbb Z^2\) subshift without periodic points and let \(Y\) be a \(\mathbb Z^2\) square filling mixing SFT. Then, there exists an embedding \(X \hookrightarrow Y\) if and only if \(h(X)<h(Y)\).

msc.text: Multi-dimensional shifts of finite type, tiling dynamics

title.title: Morphisms from non-periodic \(\mathbb Z^2\)-subshifts. I: Constructing embeddings from homomorphisms

editorial_contributions.text: This paper is the second of a series of papers which give a version of Krieger's embedding theorem [\textit{W. Krieger}, Ergodic Theory Dyn. Syst. 2, 195--202 (1982; Zbl 0508.54032)]. It is proved that if (A) \(X\) is a nonperiodic \(\mathbb Z^2\)-subshift (\(\sigma^vx=x \Rightarrow v=0 \in \mathbb Z^2\)) and (B) \(Y\) is a \(\mathbb Z^2\)-subshift of finite type satisfying certain mixing condition then (C) there exists a homomorphism \(X\to Y\) (a continuous shift-commuting map from \(X\) to \(Y\)). Combined with the results from the previous paper of the author [Ergodic Theory Dyn. Syst. 23, 587--609 (2003; Zbl 1031.37017)] this gives that if (A) and (B) are satisfied then an embedding (a continuous injective shift-commuting map) from \(X\) to \(Y\) exists if and only if \(h(X)<h(Y)\), where \(h\) denotes the topological entropy.

msc.text: Multi-dimensional shifts of finite type, tiling dynamics

title.title: Morphisms from non-periodic \(\mathbb{Z}^2\) subshifts. II: Constructing homomorphism to square-filling mixing shifts of finite type

editorial_contributions.text:
When dealing with minimal \(\mathbb Z\) actions, a result of M. Boyle states that two minimal \(\mathbb Z\) actions \(S\) and \(T\) on a Cantor set are suspension equivalent if and only if there are bounded orbit injections from \(S\) and \(T\) into a common \(\mathbb Z\) actions \(R\). The aim of the paper under review is to prove the above statement for minimal \(\mathbb Z^{d}\) actions.

Main result: Let \((X,T)\) and \((Y,S)\) be \(\mathbb Z^{d}\) minimal Cantor systems for \(d=1,2\). The systems \((X,T)\) and \((Y,S)\) are suspension equivalent if and only if there is a \(\mathbb Z^{d}\) minimal Cantor system \((Z,R)\) and bounded orbit injections \(h_{1}:(X,T)\rightarrow (Z,R)\) and \(h_{2}:(Y,S)\rightarrow (Z,R)\). The authors prove that the simpler direction of the main theorem also works for any \(d\geq 2\). As a consequence of the main theorem, the following result is presented: Let \((X,T)\) and \((Y,S)\) be \(\mathbb Z^{2}\) minimal Cantor systems and suppose the continuous injection \(h:X\rightarrow Y\) is a bounded orbit injection. Then \(h(X)\) is of second category in \(Y\).

msc.text: Dynamical systems involving transformations and group actions with special properties (minimality, distality, proximality, expansivity, etc.)
Multi-dimensional shifts of finite type, tiling dynamics

title.title: Bounded orbit injections and suspension equivalence for minimal \(\mathbb{Z}^2\) actions

editorial_contributions.text:
The work of \textit{D. S. Ornstein} and \textit{B. Weiss} [J. Anal. Math. 48, 1--141 (1987; Zbl 0637.28015)] suggests that the natural setting for ergodic theory are actions of countable amenable groups. The first natural examples involving non-abelian groups are actions of the discrete Heisenberg group \(H\) which is \(\mathbb{Z}^3\) with the multiplication defined by 
\[
 (x,y,x)\cdot (x',y',z')= (x+x',y+y',z+z'+xy').
\]
 Such non-abelian actions are not well understood. The purpose of this paper is to gain insight into such actions by studying Heisenberg odometers, giving a detailed geometric analysis of these actions. In the classical case (where the group acting is \(\mathbb{Z}\)), these are rank-one transformations, ergodic with rational discrete spectrum and zero entropy, and can be constructed by cutting and stacking of an interval. Odometer action have been generalized to \(\mathbb{Z}^d\)-actions with similar properties. In [J. Lond. Math. Soc., II. Ser. 78, No. 1, 1--20 (2008; Zbl 1154.54024)], \textit{M. I. Cortez} and \textit{S. Petite} generalized this theory to define odometer dynamical systems for any discrete, finitely generated and residually finite group \(G\). In this paper, the authors give a classification of Heisenberg odometers, and give examples in each class. A new proof of the result due to Mackey that general \(G\) odometers have discrete spectrum is given. Extending work of \textit{M. I. Cortez} [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. 15, No. 3, 859--881 (2006; Zbl 1130.54016)], examples of Heisenberg odometers that are not of product type are constructed, and necessary and sufficient conditions for a \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) odometer to be of product type are given.

msc.text: General groups of measure-preserving transformations and dynamical systems
Ergodic theorems, spectral theory, Markov operators
